ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure is generator G1, labeled 15 kV; on the right side is generator G2, labeled 15 kV. The two generators are connected by one line, with bus 3 at the midpoint. The left line section L1 goes from the G1 side to bus 3, labeled 10 km; the right line section L2 goes from bus 3 to the G2 side, labeled 10 km. Therefore bus 3 is fed from the generators on both sides through their respective line sections. Reasoning: According to the specified method, take the common base as 100 MVA, 15 kV. The reactance of G1 is 0.25 pu on 250 MVA, converted to 100 MVA as 0.25 × 100/250 = 0.10 pu. The reactance of G2 is 0.10 pu on 100 MVA, already on the common base, so it remains 0.10 pu. Each line section has length 10 km, and the reactance is 10 × 0.225 = 2.25 Ω. Under the 100 MVA, 15 kV base, Z_base = 15^2/100 = 2.25 Ω, so the reactance of each line section is 2.25/2.25 = 1.0 pu. The branch reactance looking from bus 3 toward G1 is 1.0 + 0.10 = 1.10 pu; the branch reactance looking from bus 3 toward G2 is also 1.0 + 0.10 = 1.10 pu. The Thevenin reactance of the two branches in parallel is 1.10 || 1.10 = 0.55 pu. Three-phase fault capacity = 100/0.55 = 181.82 MVA.

method.method_draft: First describe the diagram as two generators feeding bus 3 from opposite sides through line sections L1 and L2. Choose a common base, e.g. 100 MVA and 15 kV. Convert G1 reactance: 0.25 pu on 250 MVA becomes 0.25*(100/250)=0.10 pu. G2 is already 0.10 pu on 100 MVA. Convert each 10 km line: X = 10*0.225 = 2.25 ohm; on 100 MVA, 15 kV base, Z_base = 15^2/100 = 2.25 ohm, so each line is 1.0 pu. The Thevenin branch from bus 3 to G1 is 1.0+0.10=1.10 pu, and the branch to G2 is also 1.10 pu. Their parallel equivalent is 1.10||1.10 = 0.55 pu. Then three-phase fault MVA = 100/0.55 = 181.82 MVA.
